description: Phase 1 pilot questions. Expected facts are annotation targets, not answer templates.

questions.question: My contract calls me self-employed, but I have to do the work myself and my manager sets when and how I do it. What should I look at to understand my employment status?
expected_facts: Employment law recognises worker, employee, and self-employed status categories.
Relevant worker indicators can include personal service, a limited right to send a substitute, and supervision or control; these indicators do not decide an individual case on their own.
Status affects rights and employer responsibilities; the contract label alone should not be treated as a final legal decision.
Employment status for tax can differ from employment law status.
questions.answer_note: Explain relevant general factors and avoid deciding the user's legal status from a short description.

questions.question: Does my employment contract have to be written down, and when can it start?
expected_facts: An employment contract does not have to be written down.
A contract can exist as soon as a person accepts a job offer.
The written statement of employment particulars is a distinct written document covered by the guide.

questions.question: Do bank holidays have to be extra days on top of my annual leave, and how should I check that my holiday pay is right?
expected_facts: Almost all workers are entitled to 5.6 weeks of paid annual leave, subject to the guide's stated rules and limits.
An employer can include bank holidays within statutory annual leave; they do not have to be extra paid leave.
The guide has a separate holiday-pay section; the answer should explain that the calculation depends on working pattern and pay details rather than inventing a figure.
questions.answer_note: Do not calculate an individual's holiday pay without the necessary pay and working-pattern facts.

questions.question: I am an employee and have been off sick for four days. Do I need a fit note, and does being off sick automatically mean I get Statutory Sick Pay?
expected_facts: Employees off work sick for 7 days or less do not need a fit note or other healthcare-professional proof; the employer can ask for self-certification.
Being off sick does not by itself establish SSP eligibility; the separate SSP guidance sets eligibility conditions.
Do not state a current SSP rate or decide eligibility without checking the current guidance and the worker's circumstances.
questions.answer_note: The evidence should distinguish sick-leave proof rules from SSP eligibility.

questions.question: Can my employer make me work more than 48 hours a week, and what does opting out mean?
expected_facts: The guide describes a 48-hour average weekly limit for most workers, with exceptions and a reference period.
A worker can agree to opt out of the limit, and the decision must be voluntary.
questions.answer_note: Mention that the rule is an average and that the guide lists exceptions.

questions.question: My employer says my role is redundant. What should I expect about fair selection and consultation?
expected_facts: Selection should use a fair and objective method, and protected or otherwise prohibited reasons cannot be used to select someone.
The guide explains consultation rights and related redundancy processes; requirements can depend on the circumstances and number of affected employees.
questions.answer_note: Avoid deciding whether a particular selection was fair without the process details.

questions.question: I was dismissed shortly after raising a safety concern at work. Was that automatically unfair?
expected_facts: Some reasons connected with health and safety can make a dismissal automatically unfair.
Whether the protection applies depends on the facts, the worker's status, and the reason for dismissal; the source cannot determine the user's case.
questions.answer_note: Give general guidance, identify missing facts, and do not conclude that this dismissal was automatically unfair.

questions.question: Do I need a minimum length of service to take Statutory Maternity Leave, and is Statutory Maternity Pay based on the same eligibility rules?
expected_facts: Statutory Maternity Leave eligibility applies to employees who give the correct notice and does not depend on length of service, hours, or pay.
Statutory Maternity Pay has separate eligibility requirements, including a qualifying period and earnings conditions.
questions.answer_note: Separate leave eligibility from pay eligibility and avoid quoting changeable monetary thresholds.

questions.question: How much must my employer contribute to my workplace pension each month?
questions.answer_note: Pensions are outside the MVP source scope; return a clear insufficient-evidence response rather than guessing.

questions.question: Can you help me write a CV for a job?
questions.answer_note: Job-search advice is outside the v1 employment-guidance topics. Return a clear out-of-scope response.
